newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill -private.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill -private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Thursday were at a standstill before the Independence Day holiday on Friday, feedlot sources said.
"I don't look for anything to happen today. Packer's got what he needs to get things started on Monday," a Panhandle-area feedlot manager said.

There were no reported bids, but they were expected at $62.00 per cwt if any surface, several sources said. Cattle owners continued to price cattle at $63.00, steady with Tuesday's active sales in the central and southern Plains, they said.
Fed cattle prices next week were seen steady to possibly $1.00 lower amid outlooks for sluggish beef demand following the three-day holiday weekend, market sources said.
Beef demand this week was starting to slow, despite lower prices. Prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.24 to $0.75 per cwt, with 275 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Beef movement for the week to date Wednesday totaled 707 loads, compared with 889 for the same period last week.
Fed cattle prices also were expected to be pressured by increased market-ready cattle supplies projected through July, several cattle feeders said.
